questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment. a resistance of $9 \Omega$ is connected in the left gap and an unknown resistance greater than $9 \Omega$ is connected in the right gap. If the resistance in the gaps are interchanged, the balancing point shifts by 10 cm. The unknown resistance is
questions.solution:
In meter bridge experiment,
$\frac{9}{x}=\frac{1}{100-1}$ ...(i)
Again, $\frac{x}{9}=\frac{1+10}{100-(1+10)}=\frac{1+10}{90-1}$ ...(ii)
Multiplying eq(i) and (ii), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1(1+10)}{(100-1)(90-1)}=1 \Rightarrow 1^2+10 \ell=9000-1901+1^2 \\
& \therefore 1=45 \mathrm{ cm} \\
& \therefore \quad \text{ From eq(i) } \\
& \frac{9}{x}=\frac{45}{55} \Rightarrow x=11 \Omega
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $N$ divisions on the main scale of a vernier calipers coincide with $\left(N + 1\right)$ divisions of the vernier scale. If each division of main scale is $a$ units, then the least count of the calipers is
questions.solution:
It is given that $\left(N + 1\right)$ Divisions on vernier scale$\left(V . S . D .\right)$=$N$ Divisions on main scale $\left(M . S . D .\right)$
$⇒ 1V . S . D . = \dfrac{N}{N + 1}M . S . D .

Least count$ of vernier callipers$\left(L . C .\right)$ = 1M . S . D . - 1V . S . D .

$⇒ L . C . = a - a\left(\dfrac{N}{N + 1}\right) = \dfrac{a}{N + 1}unit$
